$comment: TEST FIXTURE -- the reviewer identities the CON-32 predicates were ported from, expressed as data. Every pattern here reproduces a literal that used to be written into cli/src/gates/predicates.ts in bankai-core, so src/gates/predicates.test.ts (the ported companion suite) proves the parameterised predicates behave identically to the originals. Not shipped; see ../../README.md.

reviewers.$comment: Posts as copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]; nothing re-requests it after a final push, so under the bounded policy only a PENDING request owes a round.
reviewers.name: copilot

reviewers.$comment: The check IS the round: it posts a review only when it has findings. The enrolment pattern is ANCHORED and CASE-SENSITIVE on purpose -- a sibling probe job would otherwise enrol the reviewer on every PR. It is not a DEFAULT approver, but it joins the approval set for a PR it has actually posted a review on at head -- the shell's `approvers="$approvers,bisky"` arm.
reviewers.name: bisky

reviewers.$comment: Posts under a login carrying either word depending on the installation, and its check name varies with the installation too -- hence an UNANCHORED, case-insensitive substring where bisky's is anchored.
reviewers.name: bugbot

dependabot_carve_out.$comment: CON-30's review carve-out (zheref/nen#18). The dependency bot opens pull requests nothing re-requests a review on; the repository shims the two review contexts to success instead, and this is what lets the decider READ that shim rather than each caller re-deriving the exemption. Satisfied by PRESENCE of both contexts, green -- never by their absence.
